The week that broke 3,502.78. On Friday I'm watching how far gold has recovered into last week's range.

As of 06:59 on Nov 27, XS's MT5 (XAUUSDs) is at 3,565.91. This week's high is 3,689.71 and low 3,426.61. Price went below last week's low of 3,502.78 at one point, and this morning's price is above it. When reviewing the week, I record separately "how far the range widened mid-week" and "where it is as of Friday".

[Upside: 3,600.00-3,607.08]
3,600.00 is a round number, and 3,607.08 is the high up to this morning and the most recent 4-hour peak. Price is below the 4-hour SMA20 (3,577.43), and SMA20 is also below SMA50 (3,661.92). If a 4-hour close breaks this upper band, next I watch from around SMA50 up to this week's high of 3,689.71. I want to compare how close a rebound past the recent peak gets to the previous peak.

[Downside: 3,500.00-3,502.78]
The axis for my Friday review is this band where the round number and last week's low overlap. When it tests lower again, I first record the position where the wick went outside the band, and once the candle is confirmed, check whether the close stayed inside or outside the band. If the 4-hour closes below the band, I watch how far the rebounding candles can recover between there and this week's low of 3,426.61. If it closes back at the band, I also record that position and review it after the weekend.

In my range verification, even for candles that passed the same line, I record wick and close positions separately. When price passed on both sides of last week's low, as it did this week, it makes it easier to cross-check the low left on the daily chart against the range price recovered afterwards. Trade at your own judgment.

Verification notes for weekly reviews are shared in the open chat "Hide Gold FX Study Group" in my profile.

Thinking about it again, companies investing in financial products rather than their own business probably stems from banks' reluctance to lend, real P&L deficits, etc.

With financial products running rampant, showing a profit on the P&L is something anyone can fudge these days.

Is that why the principal lock is 1 month?

It's harder to see since it's overseas FX,
but if dominoes start falling, it could go down together since it accesses the existing financial system.

The time lag when withdrawing in crypto is probably due to low inventory, well, I don't know.

If so, the structure may actually be a self-propelled operation that relies on users.

Personally I'm very grateful because I made a profit on COPYX's gold trades (though I'm deep in the red elsewhere lol).

If the company's management worsens and operations get tough, I think the 24x amplify would simply fall first, so is there a risk of withdrawal suspension?

I can't say there isn't, but I think the possibility is low.

I can't give a definite answer on this.

Compliance seems solid too, as far as the operator says.

But investments have growth, decline and eventual disappearance, so individual judgment is needed there.

I'll wait and see until the December Japan-US interest rate policy meetings.

Timing of when to stop or retreat matters.
